text:
liz: Quick proposal — we should add an "explainable unit-cost" alert per-route. Trigger when the effective unit cost (post-cache, post-batching) spikes >20% over baseline for 10m and include a short root-cause summary (cache hit change, routing fallback, model SKU shift). Anyone against?

sam: Agree on the need. Biggest question: what exactly is "effective unit cost" for the alert — infra amortized cost or token list price?

deepa: My suggestion: effective_unit_cost = (route_total_compute_cost - cache_credit) / effective_tokens_served. cache_credit = estimated_saved_tokens * price_of_original_model. We need to include batching amortization separately.

jonathan: We should avoid per-request heavy joins in OLAP. Do sampling (1-5%) and extrapolate, plus maintain a small rollup table per route/model/5m window.

liz: Example calc we can emit as a derived metric into metrics pipeline:
```
route_cost = sum(gpu_ms * gpu_cost_per_ms) + sum(cpu_ms * cpu_cost_per_ms)
cache_credit = sum(saved_output_tokens) * token_price(model_variant)
effective_unit_cost = (route_cost - cache_credit) / sum(served_tokens_after_prefix_sharing)
```
This gives a single number we can alert on.

mike: A couple of gotchas: 1) saved_output_tokens is tricky when we dedupe via prefix cache + rerank caches. 2) token_price varies by model SKU — need model tags on telemetry events.

sam: Also quota interplay: if a route hits quota fallback (lower-tier model) cost might go down but quality changes. Alert should show that fallback happened.

liz: UX idea for console alert card: show sparkline of effective_unit_cost, delta from baseline, and 3 top contributing signals: "cache hit rate down", "fallback to cheaper model", "sudden seq_len increase". Link to sampled request traces.

jonathan: Implementation plan from infra side: 1) add lightweight telemetry fields on request completion: model_sku, served_tokens, saved_tokens_estimate, gpu_ms 2) ingest into kinesis, 5m rollups in ClickHouse, 3) alerting rule reads rollups.

deepa: We'll need a consistent definition of saved_tokens_estimate — propose: saved_tokens_estimate = max(0, baseline_output_tokens - actual_output_tokens + prefix_hit_estimate). Keep it conservative.

liz: Example alert message payload (for ops/console):
```
route: /v1/generate
period: 10m
effective_unit_cost: $0.0034 (+32%)
contributors: ["cache_hit_rate -14%","fallback:model-small","median_seq_len +22%"]
traces: /console/trace/abc123 (sampled)
```

costbot: [automated] potential cost spike detected on route /v1/generate — effective_unit_cost +32% over baseline. Sam, liz tagged for follow-up. :warning:

mike: For accuracy we should store model_sku at request time and keep a small history table for price lookups. Also watch out for quantized model variants where token_price differs but performance is similar.

jonathan: On sampling: capture full traces for 1 in 200 requests, but emit the derived rollup metrics for every request (cheap counters). Sampling will give root-cause traces without huge storage.

sam: One more edge: cross-route cache sharing (shared prefix cache across routes) — when we credit cache savings, we need attribution rules (split proportional to tokens requested, or to route weight). Otherwise teams will get weird credits.

deepa: Agreed. Start with proportional token-share attribution in rollups, document the heuristic in console. We can add a "cache-credit detail" drilldown in the UI to show attribution assumptions.

liz: Action items:
- deepa + jonathan: draft telemetry fields + rollup schema (this week)
- mike: price lookup table + model_sku tagging (this sprint)
- sam + liz: console card mock and alert wording (next sprint)
- infra-bot: create a spike ticket and assign owners

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-3245: "Explainable effective-unit-cost alerts per-route" and assigned to deepa, jonathan, mike. ETA: triage meeting Friday.

sam: Sounds good. If we keep the math conservative we can avoid noisy alerts. Also add a cooldown so repeated spikes don't spam.

liz: Perfect. I'll add a short doc to the product board with examples and expected signals. Thanks all :rocket:
